description: A single-panel optical micrograph (no sub-panels) of the hot-rolled Fe-30Mn-9Al-1.01Si 0.9C-0.5Mo alloy in the peak aged condition (60 h at 530 °C), imaged with differential interference contrast (DIC) after nital etching; the whole field carries the blue tint typical of DIC rendering. A white scale bar in the lower-right corner is labelled "20 µm". The field is filled by an equiaxed polygonal grain structure whose grains are on the order of the scale-bar length; grain boundaries appear as sharp, dark, preferentially etched lines, locally thickened into dark beaded boundaries where contrast is strongest. Grain interiors are largely featureless pale blue-grey, with faint parallel striations in some grains. Faint, darker diffuse bands several grains wide cross the field diagonally. No axes, legend, colour scale or numeric annotation other than the scale bar is present. The caption states the preferential grain-boundary etching is caused by j-carbide (κ-carbide) precipitation and the banding by alloy segregation; the citing text states the plates were hot rolled at 900 °C to 84% reduction, solution treated 10 min at 900 °C and water quenched to give this equiaxed structure of 10-20 µm average grain diameter, and that peak-aging grain-boundary κ-carbide lowered elongation from 54% to 14%.

observations.observation: The figure is a single-panel optical micrograph of a polygonal, fully recrystallised-looking grain structure with no sub-panels and no axes or legend.
A white scale bar annotated "20 µm" is printed in the lower-right corner of the micrograph.
Grain boundaries are imaged as dark, strongly etched continuous lines that locally thicken into dark beaded boundaries, indicating preferential boundary attack.
Grain interiors are largely uniform pale blue-grey, with faint parallel striations visible in some grains.
Diffuse darker bands several grain-widths across run diagonally through the field, in addition to the sharp grain-boundary network.
The caption states the material is the hot-rolled Fe-30Mn-9Al-1.01Si 0.9C-0.5Mo alloy in the peak aged condition (60 h at 530 °C).
The caption states the preferential grain-boundary etching is due to j-carbide (κ-carbide) precipitation and that the banding results from alloy segregation.
The caption states the specimen was imaged using differential interference contrast techniques and etched with nital.

The citing text states cast plates were hot rolled at 900 °C to an 84% reduction in thickness, solution treated for 10 min at 900 °C and water quenched to produce an equiaxed grain structure 10 µm to 20 µm in average diameter, as shown in this figure.
The citing text states that peak aging produced κ-carbide precipitation on grain boundaries and lowered elongation from 54% to 14%.

unreadable_items: no numeric grain-size values are printed on the image; grain size must be judged against the 20 µm scale bar
the faint intra-granular striations are too low in contrast to attribute (slip traces vs. annealing twins vs. etching artefact) at the supplied resolution
